label: Microsoft Teams
description: Read chats, channel conversations, meetings, and transcripts, and create meeting links.
securityDescription: Microsoft Teams sign-in opens through Composio. Agents read what the signed-in person can see: their chats, the teams and channels they belong to, channel and chat messages, files found by search, and their online meetings with recording lists and transcripts. With write access, Agents can only create a standalone online meeting the person organizes, including its lobby and recording options; nobody is invited or notified. Agents cannot post, edit, pin, or delete messages, start chats, add or remove members, create, archive, or delete teams or channels, change team, channel, chat, or tab settings, set presence, or change shifts.

capabilities.description: Lists a specified user's Microsoft Teams chats, supporting filtering and property selection. An unfiltered first page for `user_id='me'` includes the personal self-chat with `is_self_chat=true`; use SEND_MESSAGE_TO_SELF and LIST_MESSAGES_TO_SELF for it. Returns one provider page per call (up to `top`, further bounded by `limit` if given), potentially plus that one synthetic entry, and a `next_page_token`.

top.description: The number of provider chats to return per page (1-50). Microsoft Graph enforces a maximum of 50 per request. An unfiltered first page for user_id='me' can contain one additional synthetic self-chat. This action returns ONE page per call plus a `next_page_token`; pass that token back as `page_token` to get the next page.

limit.description: Caps how many provider chats this single call returns (bounds the page size). An unfiltered first page for user_id='me' can contain one additional synthetic self-chat beyond this limit. If more chats match than `limit`, the response includes a `next_page_token` — pass it back as `page_token` to fetch the rest; nothing is dropped. When larger than one Graph page (max 50) a single call still returns one page plus a token. Leave unset to return a full page.

filter.description: OData filter query string (do not include '$filter='). Supports filtering by chat properties like 'topic', 'chatType' (e.g., "chatType eq 'group'", "topic eq 'Project X'"), and 'installedApps/any(...)' for app-based filtering. The synthetic self-chat is included only when this is empty because its filter semantics cannot be safely emulated.

select.description: A list of specific Microsoft Graph chat resource properties to retrieve (e.g., 'id', 'topic'). If omitted or empty, a default set of properties is returned. Each string in the list should be a valid property name.

user_id.description: The ID or user principal name (UPN) of the user whose chats are to be retrieved. Use 'me' to specify the currently authenticated user. An unfiltered first-page request for 'me' includes the user's self-chat (personal notes); use SEND_MESSAGE_TO_SELF to add a note or LIST_MESSAGES_TO_SELF to read it without supplying IDs.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend the same required identifier (user_id), but filter/select params need not be repeated — the token carries them.

capabilities.description: Search files in Microsoft Teams using KQL syntax. Find files by name, type, content, author, and modification date across all Teams and channels. Supports boolean logic and date ranges. Examples: 'filetype:pdf AND lastmodifiedtime>=2024-10-01', 'contract AND budget', 'filename:report AND author:user@example.com'

size.description: The maximum number of file results to return per page. Use with from_index for pagination.

query.description: Search query for files in Teams. Supports keywords, filenames, and content search. **Basic Syntax:** - Keywords: 'budget contract' - Exact phrases: '"project timeline"' - Filenames: 'report.pdf' or 'filename:contract' - File types: 'filetype:pdf' or 'filetype:docx' - Boolean: 'contract AND budget' or 'report OR summary' **Property Filters:** - filename: File name - 'filename:contract' - filetype: File extension - 'filetype:pdf', 'filetype:docx', 'filetype:xlsx' - author: Creator -

region.description: Specifies the geographic region for the search request. ONLY required when using application permissions (S2S authentication). DO NOT use with delegated permissions (user authentication) - the API will reject the request. Valid values: 'NAM' (North America), 'EMEA' (Europe, Middle East, Africa), 'APAC' (Asia Pacific). Leave unset (None) for delegated permissions.

from_index.description: The 0-based starting index for pagination. To paginate: check response['value'][0]['hitsContainers'][0]['moreResultsAvailable']. If true, call again with from_index += size (e.g., 0 → 25 → 50).

input.description: Searches files in Microsoft Teams using the Microsoft Search API.

capabilities.description: Search Microsoft Teams messages using KQL syntax. Supports sender (from:), date filters (sent:), attachments, and boolean logic. Works across all Teams chats and channels the user has access to, including matching self-DM/personal-note messages whose resource chatId is `48:notes`. Examples: 'from:user@example.com AND sent>=2024-10-01', 'punchlist OR termination', 'sent>today-30 AND hasattachment:yes' NOTE: This action requires an organizational Microsoft 365 account (Azure AD/Entra ID). It does NOT work with personal Microsoft accounts (MSA) such as @outlook.com, @hotmail.com, or @live.com. If using a personal Microsoft account, this search will fail.

size.description: The maximum number of search results to return per page. Use with from_index for pagination.

query.description: KQL (Keyword Query Language) search query string. Supports advanced syntax for precise searches. **Basic Syntax:** - Simple keywords: 'budget report' - Exact phrases: '"quarterly review"' - Boolean operators: 'urgent AND deadline' or 'invoice OR receipt' **Property Filters (prefix:value):** - from: Sender - 'from:user@example.com' or 'from:example.com' - sent: Date sent - 'sent:2024-10-01', 'sent>=2024-10-01', 'sent:2024-10-01..2024-10-31', 'sent>today-7' - hasattachment: Has files -

region.description: Specifies the geographic region for the search request. ONLY required when using application permissions (S2S authentication). DO NOT use with delegated permissions (user authentication) - the API will reject the request. Valid values: 'NAM' (North America), 'EMEA' (Europe, Middle East, Africa), 'APAC' (Asia Pacific). Leave unset (None) for delegated permissions.

from_index.description: The 0-based starting index for pagination. To paginate: check response['value'][0]['hitsContainers'][0]['moreResultsAvailable']. If true, call again with from_index += size (e.g., 0 → 25 → 50). The Teams message ID is hits[]['resource']['id']; hits[]['hitId'] is only the search result's internal identifier.

enable_top_results.description: If `true`, sorts results by relevance; otherwise, sorts by date in descending order (newest first).

input.description: Searches Microsoft Teams messages using the Microsoft Search API.

capabilities.description: Retrieves Microsoft Teams accessible by the authenticated user, allowing filtering, property selection, and pagination.

top.description: Maximum number of teams to return per page (1-999). Used for pagination; see `next_link` in response.

count.description: When true, includes the total count of items in the @odata.count property in the response. The count is only returned in the first page of results.

filter.description: OData v4.0 filter string to refine results based on team properties (e.g., `startsWith(displayName,'A')`). Consult OData v4.0 documentation for syntax.

select.description: Comma-separated team properties to retrieve (e.g., 'id,displayName,description'). If empty or omitted, standard properties are returned. Supported properties include `id`, `displayName`, `description`, `visibility`.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend the same required identifier(s) (none), but filter/sort/search params need not be repeated — the token carries them.

capabilities.description: Tool to list messages in a Teams channel when team_id and channel_id are known (no chat_id required). Use this to enumerate channel message history and obtain message_id for follow-on operations like listing replies or getting message details.

top.description: Maximum number of messages to return per page (1-50). Microsoft Graph enforces a maximum of 50 messages per request.

expand.description: Optional expansion parameter. Only 'replies' is supported, which includes message replies (up to 1,000 per message; use replies@odata.nextLink for more).

team_id.description: Unique identifier (GUID) of the Microsoft Teams team.

channel_id.description: Unique identifier of the channel within the team.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend the same required identifiers (team_id, channel_id), but filter/sort params need not be repeated — the token carries them.

input.description: Request schema for listing messages in a Teams channel.

capabilities.description: Retrieves channels for a specified Microsoft Teams team ID (must be valid and for an existing team), with options to include shared channels, filter results, and select properties.

filter.description: OData v4 query string to filter channels (e.g., `startswith(displayName,'Sales')` or `membershipType eq 'private'`).

select.description: Comma-separated channel properties to return (e.g., 'id,displayName,description'); empty for default properties. Common: `id`, `displayName`, `description`, `email`, `membershipType`, `webUrl`.

team_id.description: Unique identifier (GUID/UUID) of the Microsoft Teams team. Must be in UUID format (e.g., '87b0560f-fc0d-4442-add8-b380ca926707'). Team names are not accepted. Use MICROSOFT_TEAMS_LIST_USER_JOINED_TEAMS to get team IDs.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend the same required identifier (team_id), but filter/select params need not be repeated — the token carries them.

include_shared_channels.description: If true, include channels shared with the team (uses allChannels endpoint). If false, exclude shared channels from results by filtering on membershipType.

capabilities.description: Return the identity (email, name) of the connected Microsoft Teams account.

input.description: The current connected account's identity. Takes no parameters.
